actions-list.actionItem: Pursuant to the order of yesterday, the Journal of the proceedings of the Senate was deemed approved to date.
Pursuant to the order of yesterday,the morning hour being deemed expired, and the times for the recognition of the two leaders being reserved.
The following transactions of morning business occurred on today.

H.R. 2347 (Rep. Smucker):
        A bill to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to exclude from gross income any damages, other than punitive damages, received on account of any sexual acts or sexual contact.

        -- Motion to proceed to consideration of measure agreed to in Senate by Yea-Nay Vote. 62 - 21. Record Vote Number: 258 


        -- Measure laid before Senate by motion.

        -- Motion by Senator Thune to commit to Senate Committee on Finance with instructions to report back forthwith with the following amendment (SA 6888) made in Senate.
 

 S.Amdt. 6883 (Sen. Capito):
        In the nature of a substitute.

        --Amendment SA 6883 proposed by Senator Thune for Senator Capito.


 S.Amdt. 6884 (Sen. Thune):
        To improve the bill.

        --Amendment SA 6884 proposed by Senator Thune to Amendment SA 6883.


 S.Amdt. 6885 (Sen. Thune):
        To improve the bill.

        --Amendment SA 6885 proposed by Senator Thune to Amendment SA 6884.


 S.Amdt. 6886 (Sen. Thune):
        To improve the bill.

        --Amendment SA 6886 proposed by Senator Thune to language proposed to be stricken by amendment no. 6883.


 S.Amdt. 6887 (Sen. Thune):
        To improve the bill.

        --Amendment SA 6887 proposed by Senator Thune to Amendment SA 6886.


 S.Amdt. 6888 (Sen. Thune):
        To improve the bill.

        --Amendment SA 6888 proposed by Senator Thune.


 S.Amdt. 6889 (Sen. Thune):
        To improve the bill.

        --Amendment SA 6889 proposed by Senator Thune to Amendment SA 6888 (the instructions of the motion to commit).


 S.Amdt. 6890 (Sen. Thune):
        To improve the bill.

        --Amendment SA 6890 proposed by Senator Thune to Amendment SA 6889.




 H.R. 4930 (Rep. Moore):
        A bill to expand the sharing of information with respect to suspected violations of intellectual property rights in trade.

        -- Senate Committee on Finance discharged by Unanimous Consent.

        -- Passed Senate without amendment by Unanimous Consent.


 S. 2434 (Sen. Husted):
        A bill to amend the Dayton Aviation Heritage Preservation Act of 1992 to adjust the boundary of the Dayton Aviation Heritage National Historical Park, and for other purposes.

        -- Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources discharged by Unanimous Consent.

        -- Passed Senate without amendment by Unanimous Consent.


 S. 3720 (Sen. Schiff):
        A bill to amend the National Trails System Act to direct the Secretary of the Interior to conduct a study on the feasibility of designating the Bay Area Ridge as a national scenic trail, and for otherpurposes.

        -- Passed Senate with an amendment by Unanimous Consent.


 S. 3923 (Sen. Cruz):
        A bill to improve the weather research of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, support improvements in weather forecasting and prediction, and expand commercial opportunities forthe provision of weather data.

        -- Measure laid before Senate by unanimous consent.

        -- The committee amendments withdrawn by Unanimous Consent.

        -- Passed Senate with an amendment by Unanimous Consent.
 

 S.Amdt. 6881 (Sen. Cruz):
        No Statement of Purpose on File.

        --Amendment SA 6881 proposed by Senator Barrasso for Senator Cruz.

        --Amendment SA 6881 agreed to in Senate by Unanimous Consent.




 S.Res. 472 (Sen. Wicker):
        A resolution supporting the designation of October30 as the "International Day of Political Prisoners".

        -- Senate Committee on Foreign Relations discharged by Unanimous Consent.

        -- Resolution agreed to in Senate without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent.


 S.Res. 950 (Sen. Collins):
        A resolution designating the week of September 14 through September 18, 2026, as "National Clean Energy Week".

        -- Senate Committee on the Judiciary discharged by Unanimous Consent.

        -- Resolution agreed to in Senate without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent.


 S.Res. 951 (Sen. Hyde-Smith):
        A resolution designating September 2026 as "National Infant Mortality Awareness Month", raising awareness of infant mortality, and increasing efforts to reduce infant mortality.

        -- Senate Committee on the Judiciary discharged by Unanimous Consent.

        -- Resolution agreed to in Senate without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent.


 S.Res. 955 (Sen. Moran):
        A resolution permitting the collection of clothing, toys, food, and housewares during the holiday season for charitable purposes in Senate buildings.

        -- Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment by Unanimous Consent.
